lede: Mark won on Thursday and then lost everything else. San Francisco dropped its first game of the season in Atlanta, Baltimore gave up thirty-five unanswered to Cincinnati, Las Vegas was down 28-6 at half — one point from four. Jon could not take advantage, getting only Pittsburgh. The man who did was Bill, three from three with Dallas still to play tonight, and the table behind the leader has gone from a chase to a scrum.

beats.text: Bill against Anthony, 8:15, the last point of Week 7. Dallas is favored by four and a half on the road in a division game, which is what happens when the home team has lost four straight scoring 58 points total and is starting Tanner McKee — Jalen Hurts is on injured reserve with blood clots in his calf and lungs and is expected to miss the season. Saquon Barkley is questionable but practiced in full on Saturday for the first time since the hamstring, and Dallas ranks 30th in defense. Bill wins and he has had the week of his season; Anthony wins and he is off the bottom of the pack.

The 49ers were 6-0 and lost 29-20 in Atlanta, leading 14-3 before giving up 23 straight — they outgained the Falcons 400 to 295 and turned it over four times, Brock Purdy throwing two interceptions and George Kittle fumbling it away at the end. Baltimore led Cincinnati 13-0 at halftime and lost 35-13, giving up five straight touchdown drives with Lamar Jackson out a third week and Joe Burrow going 16-of-18 after the break. Las Vegas trailed the Rams 28-6 at half. Only Thursday saved him, and the lead is two.

A fortnight ago he was blanked and last in points per week. Cincinnati put 35 on Baltimore. Tampa Bay beat Carolina 43-13 on 258 rushing yards, a blocked field goal returned for a touchdown and a strip-sack returned for another, with Baker Mayfield back from the thumb and barely needed. The Giants beat Houston in overtime with J.J. McCarthy making his first start for them and Devin Singletary winning it from 30 yards. Nine and a half to twelve and a half in one afternoon, and he still has Dallas.

And it was not close: 20-3 in Seattle, the first game of Patrick Mahomes' career in which the Chiefs never reached the red zone, and only the second full game of his career without a touchdown pass. Jaxon Smith-Njigba caught nine for 150. Kenneth Walker III got 36 yards against the team that traded him. Tennessee led Cleveland 14-0 and lost on a last-second field goal despite Tony Pollard's 129 yards and three touchdowns. Buffalo was on bye. Pittsburgh beat New Orleans in Paris, and that was the week.

beats.tag: The pack · Five points, six owners
beats.text: Second through seventh now covers five points. Patrick is up to fourteen on Cleveland and Detroit, who beat Green Bay on a field goal at the whistle after Trey Smack missed twice. Harrison has Minnesota, the last unbeaten team in the league. Brian took Atlanta and Seattle, the two biggest results of the day. Zach beat the Jets with Miami's first win of the season and put 35 on Las Vegas without Davante Adams and on his fourth kicker. Nobody in that group is more than three points from anybody else in it.
